subtitle: Where a queen carved numbers into the mountain wind

panels.shot: epic wide of mountain pass at dawn, low-angle toward carved cave mouth
panels.action: Queen Nayanika stands poised at the lip of Naneghat’s cliffside cave, veiled but crowned, the Western Ghats falling away into mist and the ancient trade road snaking below.

dialogue.text: In the cool winds of Naneghat, Queen Nayanika of the Satavahanas carved her line, her sacrifices, and early number signs into living rock, as the Deccan first rose to power.

i18n.hi: नानेघाट की ठंडी हवा में सातवाहन रानी नयनिका ने अपनी वंशरेखा, यज्ञ और शुरुआती अंकों के चिन्ह जीवित पत्थर में काटे, जब दक्कन पहली बार ताकतवर उठा।

panels.shot: high bird’s-eye sweeping along the Western Ghats ridge
panels.action: The camera glides over rugged, forested ridges of the Western Ghats, clouds catching on peaks, while a narrow stone-cut pass cuts through the mountain wall toward the plateau.

dialogue.text: Here the Western Ghats stand like a stone curtain between sea and plateau. In their flank, Naneghat opens—a cleft of trade and tribute linking Sopara and Kalyan to Nasik and Pratishthana.

i18n.hi: यहाँ पश्चिमी घाट समंदर और पठार के बीच पत्थर की परदों जैसे खड़े हैं। उनके पेट में नानेघाट खुलता है—सोपारा‑कल्याण को नासिक‑प्रतिष्ठान से जोड़ने वाली व्यापार और कर की दरार।

panels.shot: mid-wide of caravan threading through the pass
panels.action: A long caravan of ox-carts, horses, and merchants winds through the narrow rock-cut pass, below sheer walls scarred by earlier cutting, monsoon stains darkening the stone.

dialogue.text: Salt and textiles from coastal marts, beads and grain from the plateau, iron, incense, and ideas all pass through this notch in stone. Naneghat is a lifeline of the early Deccan.

i18n.hi: तट के बाजारों का नमक‑कपड़ा, पठार के मनके‑अनाज, लोहा, धूप और विचार सब इसी पत्थर की खाई से गुजरते हैं। नानेघाट शुरुआती दक्कन की जीवनरेखा है।

panels.shot: slow push-in toward the cave façade with unfinished pillars
panels.action: The view settles on a rock-cut cave with a simple façade, rough pillars and benches inside, its walls carefully smoothed yet bearing scars of tools and patches of damage.

dialogue.text: Not a monastery, not a palace, but a place of passage and memory. A cave beside the toll, cut and endowed by a queen who chose stone and script instead of drums alone.

i18n.hi: न मठ, न महल—ये है रास्ते और याद की जगह। चुंगी के पास की गुफा, जिसे उस रानी ने कटवाया जो ढोलों की जगह पत्थर और लिपि को चुनती है।

panels.shot: medium shot inside cave, low-angle toward Nayanika watching scribes
panels.action: Queen Nayanika stands with composed authority inside the cave, jewelry modest yet royal, watching scribes squat by lamplight, tracing Brahmi letters onto the smoothed wall with brushes.

dialogue.text: She is Nayanika—read also Naganika in later eyes—wife of Satakarni, mother of princes, and likely regent over Satavahana lands in the late second to early first century before the Common Era.

i18n.hi: वह है नयनिका—बाद के लेखों में नागनिका भी—सातकर्णि की पत्नी, राजकुमारों की माँ, और शायद ईसा‑पूर्व दूसरी‑पहली सदी की सातवाहन रानी और संरक्षिका।

panels.shot: close-up on Nayanika’s profile and a scribe’s hand sketching Brahmi
panels.action: A close view of Nayanika’s steady profile, eyes intent, as beside her a scribe’s hand outlines curving Brahmi letters in black on the stone before chiselling.

dialogue.speaker: queen_nayanika
dialogue.text: Write in our Maharashtri tongue. Let those who pass hear my house as their own speech.

i18n.hi: लिखो हमारी महाराष्‍ट्री भाषा में। जो यहाँ से गुज़रे, मेरे घर को अपनी ही बोली में सुनें।

panels.shot: medium shot, Nayanika overseeing ritual preparations outside cave
panels.action: Outside the cave, Nayanika watches priests and attendants arrange vessels, ladles, and garlands, a sacrificial post rising beyond, smoke from past rites lingering faintly in the air.

dialogue.text: She orders that Vedic sacrifices already performed be recorded—rajasuya, perhaps ashvamedha—grand rites that kings used to proclaim reach and legitimacy across the plains and plateaus.

i18n.hi: वह कहती है कि किए गए वैदिक यज्ञ दर्ज करो—राजसूय, शायद अश्वमेध—वे महायज्ञ जिनसे राजा मैदानों और पठारों पर अपनी पहुँच और हक जताते थे।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Nayanika speaking to a priest and an official
panels.action: Nayanika stands between a white-clad priest and a leather-scroll-bearing official, hand lightly raised in measured command as the toll structure looms behind them.

dialogue.speaker: queen_nayanika
dialogue.text: The gifts, the cattle, the coins—record each. Not for praise alone, but so truth may stand when we are dust.

i18n.hi: दान, पशु, सिक्के—हर एक दर्ज करो। केवल बड़ाई के लिए नहीं, ताकि हम मिट्टी बन जाएँ तब भी सच खड़ा रहे।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on inscription area with early numerals and letters
panels.action: The camera presses close to the rock wall where neat Brahmi lines and small numeral-like signs take shape, a chisel poised above them, Nayanika’s shadow falling over the stone.

dialogue.text: On this wall, Maharashtri Prakrit flows in Brahmi letters, naming sacrifices and gifts, and beside them some of the earliest digit shapes that will lie behind our later written numbers.

i18n.hi: इस दीवार पर महाराष्‍ट्री प्राकृत ब्राह्मी अक्षरों में बहता है, यज्ञ और दान गिनता है, और साथ में वही शुरुआती अंक‑आकार दिखता है जो आगे चलकर हमारी संख्याएँ बनेगा।

panels.shot: medium shot inside cave with outlines of royal portraits on wall
panels.action: Inside the cave, faint carved outlines of royal figures—king, queen, princes—are visible along the wall, some faces damaged, while Nayanika studies them with a quiet, inward gaze.

dialogue.text: Portraits of Satakarni, Nayanika, their sons were carved here. Time and later hands have worn and broken them, yet even broken outlines still bear witness to a family’s claim.

i18n.hi: यहाँ सातकर्णि, नयनिका और उनके पुत्रों की मूर्तियाँ उकेरी थीं। समय और हाथों ने उन्हें घिसकर तोड़ दिया, फिर भी टूटी रेखाएँ भी उस परिवार के दावे की गवाही देती हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Nayanika’s face, light from cave mouth rim-lighting her
panels.action: Nayanika stands near the cave mouth, half in shadow and half in bright mountain light, lips set as if in silent resolve, the wind lifting the edge of her veil.

dialogue.text: Satakarni’s reign has passed. Their sons are young. In this interval, many scholars see Nayanika as regent—holding together coastal trade routes and inland strongholds while the line steadies.

i18n.hi: सातकर्णि का राज बीत गया। बेटे अभी कच्चे हैं। इस बीच कई विद्वान नयनिका को संरक्षिका मानते हैं—समुद्री व्यापार मार्ग और अंदरूनी गढ़ संभालती हुई, जब वंश अपनी पकड़ जमा रहा था।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nayanika watching merchants at toll station
panels.action: From a raised stone platform, Nayanika looks down over toll collectors weighing coins and goods, as merchants present bags and animals at the narrow bottleneck of the pass.

dialogue.text: Naneghat’s toll is more than revenue. It is a message: Satavahana authority stands at the hinge between sea and interior, counting wealth and binding routes under a single name.

i18n.hi: नानेघाट की चुंगी सिर्फ आमदनी नहीं। यह ऐलान है: सातवाहन सत्ता समंदर और भीतर के मोड़ पर खड़ी है, दौलत गिनती हुई और रास्तों को एक ही नाम के नीचे बाँधती हुई।

panels.shot: close-up on Nayanika’s hand resting on carved genealogy text
panels.action: Her hand, adorned with simple bangles, rests gently on a section of the inscription where a genealogy line runs, the grooves of the letters crisp yet shallow.

dialogue.text: So she has the genealogy cut—father, husband, sons—nesting Satavahana power among known lineages, anchoring new rule in the language and ritual of the regions it claims.

i18n.hi: तो वह वंशावली कटवाती है—पिता, पति, पुत्र—ताकि सातवाहन ताकत जानी‑पहचानी कुलों में बसे, नए राज को उसी भाषा और कर्मकांड में जड़ दे जिसका ये इलाक़ा दावा है।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide, seasons shifting around the cave
panels.action: The cave mouth and pass are shown as clouds race, rains fall, and dry seasons return, caravans changing in dress and goods while the carved letters remain fixed on the wall.

dialogue.text: Years pass. Monsoon roar, dry dust, generations of traders. Dynasties beyond the Satavahanas will come and go, yet the cave, the script, and its numbers sit silent, enduring weather and footsteps.

i18n.hi: साल गुजरते हैं। बरसात की गड़गड़ाहट, सूखी धूल, पीढ़ी‑दर‑पीढ़ी व्यापारी। सातवाहनों के आगे की वंशियाँ आएँगी‑जाएँगी; पर गुफा, लेख और उसके अंक चुपचाप हवा और कदमों को झेलते रहेंगे।

panels.shot: medium shot of later visitors examining weathered inscription
panels.action: Centuries later, cloaked travelers and local readers stand before the weathered wall, fingers tracing faint Brahmi lines and worn portrait outlines, trying to sound out the ancient Prakrit.

dialogue.text: Long after Nayanika’s own story is forgotten in common speech, the inscription remains. It becomes a puzzle for later eyes, a quarry for memory when oral tales thin and scatter.

i18n.hi: बहुत बाद में, जब बोलचाल में नयनिका की कहानी धुंधला जाती है, लेख रह जाता है। वह बाद की आँखों के लिए पहेली बनता है, जब मौखिक कथाएँ पतली पड़कर बिखरती हैं तब यादों की खान।

panels.shot: scholarly close-up of 19th-century notebook beside the inscription
panels.action: A 19th-century scholar kneels by the wall, notebook open, copying Brahmi lines by lamplight, early numerals sketched carefully, the rough stone filling his field of view.

dialogue.text: In our own time, careful epigraphers document each stroke. They debate dates and titles, study palaeography, and note that these digit signs hint at later numeral forms without yet forming a full place-value system.

i18n.hi: आज हमारे समय में धीरजवान शिलालेख‑विद् हर रेखा दर्ज करते हैं। वे तारीख‑उपाधियों पर बहस करते हैं, लिखावट पर नज़र दौड़ाते हैं, और बताते हैं कि ये अंक‑चिन्ह आगे की संख्याओं की झलक हैं, अभी पूरा स्थान‑मान तंत्र नहीं।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on a single numeral sign carved in rock
panels.action: The frame tightens on one small numeral-like mark beside the text, its groove dark with shadow, worn yet still distinct against the rugged surface.

dialogue.text: This small mark is neither zero nor our modern script, yet it is a step on the long road of Indian numbers—evidence of how administration, sacrifice, and trade demanded count and record.

i18n.hi: ये छोटा चिह्न न शून्य है, न हमारी आधुनिक लिपि, फिर भी भारतीय संख्याओं की लंबी राह का एक कदम है—सबूत कि राजकार, यज्ञ और व्यापार को गिनती और लेखा चाहिए था।

panels.shot: artful overlay: Nayanika’s ghostly figure over present-day cave
panels.action: The present-day cave and pass fill the frame, with a faint, respectful overlay of Nayanika’s figure watching from the side, her gaze turned toward the inscription and the road.

dialogue.text: We remember her not through court poems or bronze statues, but through this mountain chamber of Prakrit and stone. A queen at a toll pass, counting gifts and kings with care.

i18n.hi: हम उसे न दरबार की कविताओं से याद करते हैं, न कांस्य प्रतिमाओं से, बल्कि इस पहाड़ी प्राकृत‑पत्थर की कोठरी से। चुंगी‑मार्ग की रानी, जो यज्ञ और राजाओं को ध्यान से गिनती है।

panels.shot: final wide shot from within cave looking out onto road and horizon
panels.action: From deep inside the cave, the view looks out onto the bright pass, tiny modern figures and paths below, the inscription’s shadowed wall framing the opening to the world.

dialogue.text: Names carved with care can outlive armies. At Naneghat, Nayanika’s record stands—binding sea to plateau, ritual to rule, and early signs of number to the long memory of the Deccan.

i18n.hi: जिन नामों को सलीके से काटा जाए, वे सेनाओं से ज़्यादा जीते हैं। नानेघाट में नयनिका का लेख खड़ा है—समंदर को पठार से, यज्ञ को राज से, और संख्या के शुरुआती चिन्हों को दक्कन की लंबी स्मृति से बाँधता हुआ।

title_i18n.en: The Queen at the Coin Pass

subtitle_i18n.en: Where a queen carved numbers into the mountain wind
subtitle_i18n.hi: जहाँ एक रानी ने पहाड़ी हवाओं में अंक उकेरे
